title: Orbits SPA: initial orbit determination from 3 nights of RA/Dec (Gauss & Laplace)
description:
WHY: Demonstrate that three angles-only observations (RA/Dec at three times) determine a Keplerian heliocentric orbit, using the two classical methods (Laplace 1780, Gauss 1801). The app helps plan and record real observations, computes the orbit both ways, visualizes each method's mechanics, and compares results to published elements for well-known bodies.

HIGH-LEVEL DESIGN (decisions taken by the planner; flagged so the human can override):
- Stack: Vite + React 18 + TypeScript (strict) + Vitest. 3D via three + @react-three/fiber + @react-three/drei. State via zustand. Hash routing (react-router HashRouter) so the build is static-hostable. Charts in plain SVG (no chart lib).
- Layout: src/astro/** = pure TypeScript astronomy core, no React/DOM imports, 100% unit-tested. src/ui/** = React. src/data/** = bundled JSON datasets. tests/fixtures/** = JPL golden data.
- Units/frames: distances AU, time days, GM_sun = k^2 with Gaussian k = 0.01720209895. Internal frame = ICRF/J2000 mean equatorial. Orbital elements reported in J2000 ecliptic (to match JPL SBDB). Times: user enters UTC; core works in TT Julian Date (TT-UTC from a leap-second table + 32.184 s).
- Earth position: JPL Standish 'Approximate Positions of the Planets' Keplerian elements+rates (1800-2050 table), Earth-Moon barycenter used for Earth (~3e-5 AU error, accepted). Same table provides planets (Mars, Jupiter, ...) as catalog bodies.
- Known-body catalog: static JSON snapshot fetched once from JPL SBDB API (live fetch from the browser is NOT planned — JPL APIs lack CORS). Snapshot includes source URL and fetch date.
- Both methods emit a structured 'trace' of intermediate quantities so visualizations can replay the algorithm step by step.
- Observer: topocentric parallax supported (site lat/lon/elev) because it matters for near-Earth objects like Eros.

AMBIGUITIES FLAGGED: precision targets are educational (arcsecond-to-arcminute), not MPC-grade; no perturbation modeling (pure two-body); no differential correction / least squares beyond 3 obs (possible follow-up epic).
close_reason: All 27 child beads closed and reviewer-passed; final suite green (324 unit, 4 e2e, lint, typecheck, build).

title: LSQ polish: convergence flag, tolerance floor, banner tolerance, honest check-residual label, stronger Ceres test
description: From .27 review. STEPS: 1. src/astro/iod/lsq.ts ~191-194: relStep is computed after up to 30 halvings so failed halving reports converged=true; track whether the accepted step reduced cost and set converged=false + 'step halving failed' warning when halving exhausts without improvement (add a test that reaches it, e.g. injected bad state). 2. lsq.ts ~201 default tol 1e-10 is below the numerical floor (Ceres seed 80, obs 0/10/20/30 d, 20 iters, RMS 0.49" flagged non-converged): use a cost-based stop (relative chi2 change < 1e-8) OR tol ~1e-8 plus a noise-floor stop like gauss; that case must converge; add as test. 3. SolvePage.tsx ~394 disagreement banner: treat LSQ RMS within 1% (or 1e-3 arcsec) as a tie -> no disagreement banner; test. 4. SolvePage.tsx ~147: LSQ column's check-obs residual is not independent (check obs is in the fit) — label it 'in fit' / show it in a muted style with a tooltip, not as validation. 5. SolvePage.tsx ~141: error text says 'Gauss/Laplace seed' but only Gauss seeds — fix wording. 6. lsq.test.ts ~100-116: Ceres noisy test: use ~100 seeds and assert strict LSQ median < Gauss median (reviewer measured over 200 seeds: Gauss 3.93e-4, LSQ 3.01e-4, LSQ lower bias and sd); fix the misleading 'near-degenerate direction' comment. Keep runtime of the test reasonable (<10 s); if too slow, 60 seeds with strict assertion if it holds, else report. DONE: tests for 1,2,3,6; gates incl e2e green.
close_reason: Passed re-review. Orchestrator accepts pred<1e-4*chi2 (not 1e-6): measured FD Jacobian noise ~4e-6*chi2 at minima; reviewer probes 1440/1440 normal starts converged within 2e-5 RMS of reference.

title: Least-squares differential correction using all observations (3 IOD + check), shown on Solve
description:
WHY (user request): the 4th observation should IMPROVE the orbit, not only break root ties. Gauss/Laplace are exactly determined from 3 obs; a batch least-squares fit over all available obs (3 + optional check, 8 equations / 6 unknowns with 4 obs) is the classical next step after IOD.

DESIGN (settled by orchestrator):
1. src/astro/iod/lsq.ts (pure, no UI): differentialCorrection(obs: Observation[] (>=3), initial: {r: Vec3, v: Vec3, jdTt: number} (equatorial, heliocentric AU, AU/day), opts?: {maxIter=20, tol=1e-10 relative step, weights?}) -> {state, elements (via stateToElements), jdTt, iterations, converged, rmsArcsec, residuals: {raCosDecArcsec, decArcsec}[] per obs, covariance?: 6x6 (from (J^T W J)^-1 * s^2, s^2 = chi2/(2N-6) when 2N>6, else omit), warnings}. Residual model: predicted RA/Dec via the SAME predictor/light-time/observer conventions as src/astro/ephemeris.ts predict (state -> two-body propagate to each obs time with light-time). Unknowns: the 6-vector state at epoch jdTt. Jacobian: central finite differences (position step ~1e-7 AU-relative, velocity step ~1e-9 AU/day-relative; document). Gauss-Newton with step halving if RMS increases; RA residual wraps at 2pi and is multiplied by cos(Dec). Equal weights default.
2. Tests: (a) noise-free synthetic 4-obs Ceres: converges, rms < 0.01 arcsec, a/e/i match catalog to 1e-6 relative; (b) with seeded noise (e.g. 1 arcsec) over many seeds (e.g. 20): median |a err| of LSQ(4 obs) is lower than Gauss(3 obs) — assert on the median, not per-seed; (c) exactly 3 obs: converges with rms ~0 and agrees with Gauss refined (within 1e-6 in a); (d) bad initial guess / hyperbolic divergence -> converged=false with warning, never throws on numeric trouble (throws only on invalid input: <3 obs, non-finite).
3. compute.ts / SolvePage: add a result column/row 'Least squares (N obs)' seeded from the Gauss result (the selected root). When multiple roots survive, run LSQ from each surviving candidate and report RMS for each in the candidates table; prefer lowest RMS when a check obs exists (consistent with the .24 auto-pick; the two criteria should agree — if they disagree, show both and a warning). Show per-observation residuals for LSQ and its RMS. Use the same epoch alignment for element errors as other columns.
4. Real data: in tests/realdata.test.ts add a case using a Horizons opposition fixture with 4+ obs (e.g. the 3 IOD dates plus one more day from the fixture) and assert LSQ errors <= the Gauss errors (or within a small epsilon) — log numbers.
5. Optionally (only if simple) a fourth series on Explore is NOT required; skip.
DONE: lsq tests pass; Solve shows the LSQ column with N and RMS; real-data LSQ case logged; npm test/lint/typecheck/build and npm run test:e2e green.

title: Observer accuracy: convert Standish EMB to geocentre (low-precision Moon) — dominant real-data error
description:
WHY: src/astro/planets.ts:63-67 earthHeliocentric = EMBary (comment 'accepted as error' ~3e-5 AU); observer.ts builds on it. The .21 control test proved this dominates real-data IOD error: Ceres 10d Gauss refined e err 0.0150 (Standish EMB) vs 0.00019 (Horizons geocentre), i 0.137 deg vs 0.0014 deg — the monthly lunar wobble corrupts the curvature Gauss/Laplace rely on.
STEPS: 1. Add a low-precision geocentric Moon position (Meeus ch.47 truncated, or the Astronomical Almanac low-precision formula, ~0.3 deg / ~1000 km is plenty) in src/astro (e.g. moon.ts), J2000 equatorial AU, with unit tests vs a Horizons Moon geocentric VECTORS fixture (fetch via scripts/fetch-data.mjs; a few dates) to < 2000 km. 2. earthHeliocentric(jdTt) = EMB - moonGeo * (mu_Moon/(mu_Earth+mu_Moon)) (mass ratio 81.3005690...). Update comment. 3. Compare against tests/fixtures/horizons/earth-ceres-opposition.json: |earth - horizons| should drop from ~2.4-4.1e-5 AU to well below 1e-5 (assert < 1.5e-5 max over 41 rows). 4. Re-run tests/realdata.test.ts; tighten tolerances to measured worst case x ~2 and update the error-budget comment and bd memory 'orbits-real-data-gauss-refined-on-horizons-opposition'. 5. Existing ephemeris tests vs Horizons (6-14 arcsec) should improve or stay; if any regress, stop and report.
DONE: Moon test passes; earth-vs-Horizons max < 1.5e-5 AU; realdata tolerances tightened with measured numbers; all gates green.

title: Optional 4th (check) observation: synthetic + manual entry, used on Solve to resolve multi-root ambiguity
description:
WHY: Gauss/Laplace use exactly 3 obs (6 numbers = 6 elements), so Charlier multi-root cases are undecidable from those 3 alone. A 4th observation is the classical tie-breaker. The IOD solvers stay 3-obs; the 4th is a CHECK observation only.

DESIGN (settled by orchestrator):
- Store (src/ui/store.ts): ObservationSet gains optional checkDraft?: RowDraft and check?: Observation. observations stays exactly 3 or [] (invariant unchanged). check is set only when checkDraft parses fully valid; otherwise undefined. importSet accepts/validates check + checkDraft (same validation as the 3 rows; absent is fine). Old persisted sets without these fields must load unchanged.
- Observe page (src/ui/pages/ObservePage.tsx): below the 3 rows, a toggle/section 'Add a 4th check observation (optional)' with one more row using the same parsing/validation as rows 1-3; its time must be strictly after... NO: any time distinct from the 3 IOD times (reject duplicate jd within 1 s). Clearing the row removes check.
- Synthetic panel: an option 'Observations: 3 | 4 (3 + check)'. With 4, generate the 3 IOD obs exactly as now, plus a check obs at t3 + (t3 - t2) (same spacing after the last night), same site/noise model, label 'Synthetic check'. Default stays 3.
- Solve page (src/ui/pages/SolvePage.tsx + src/ui/solve/compute.ts): when set.check exists, for each solver result and each surviving candidate root compute predicted topocentric/geocentric RA/Dec at check.jdUtc (reuse the existing ephemeris predictor and the check obs's site; propagate the candidate orbit two-body) and the angular separation to the check obs. Show a 'Check obs residual' column (arcsec if <3600", else degrees) in the results and in the candidates table.
- Ambiguity: if >=2 survivors and check exists, auto-select the survivor with the smallest check residual (override the largest-r2 default; the user can still pick manually). Banner text becomes: 'Resolved by 4th observation: root <i> fits the check obs to <x>; the alternative misses by <y>'. If the best residual is not at least 10x smaller than the runner-up, keep the ambiguous banner and add 'the 4th observation does not clearly separate them'. Without check: existing banner unchanged plus a hint 'Add a 4th check observation on Observe to resolve this.'

DONE-CRITERIA:
1. Unit test: Eros at the known ambiguous date (testDate+90 d, see gauss tests / bd memories) with a synthetic 4-obs set: auto-selected root is the correct one (a within 1% of catalog) and banner says resolved.
2. Unit/component tests: check row parse/validation (invalid -> check undefined; duplicate time rejected); synthetic 4-option produces 3 observations + check with t4 = t3 + (t3 - t2); persisted legacy set without check still works; importSet round-trips check.
3. Check-residual column renders for a synthetic set (residual small, < 60" for noise-free synthetic).
4. npm test, npm run lint, npm run typecheck, npm run build all pass; no regressions.

title: Real-data validation: run Gauss & Laplace on Horizons astrometric fixtures
description:
INPUT: Horizons fixtures (geocentric + site 568), gauss(), laplace(), catalog.
STEPS:
1. tests/realdata.test.ts: for each fixture body choose rows at days 0, 10, 20 (and a second triplet 0, 5, 10) of the window; build Observations with the correct site (null for 500@399; Mauna Kea coords for 568: lat 19.8262, lon -155.4740 east-negative, elev 4205 m — verify against MPC obscode list and note the source).
2. Run both methods; compare to catalog elements (propagated to the middle epoch).
3. Tolerances (FLAG: these are planner estimates — if the implementation misses them by a small factor, report the actual numbers rather than loosening silently): Gauss a rel err < 1%, e abs < 0.01, i < 0.05°; Laplace refined same; Laplace classical a rel err < 10%. Eros (NEO, large parallax) must use the topocentric fixture.
4. console.table a summary of errors per body/method/spacing so the reviewer can see real numbers.
5. If a tolerance fails, investigate light-time and TT/UTC handling first; document root cause in the bead notes if a tolerance must change (requires orchestrator approval — do not change tolerances without stating it in the report).
acceptance_criteria: Test suite passes with documented tolerances on real (perturbed, real-Earth) Horizons data for Ceres, Vesta and Eros; a markdown-free summary is printed to the test log; npm test green.

title: Solve & Compare page: run Gauss and Laplace, compare to catalog elements and residuals
description:
INPUT: Observe page/store sets, gauss(), laplace(), catalog, predict().
STEPS:
1. src/ui/pages/SolvePage.tsx: select observation set and comparison target (default set.targetId; 'none' allowed). Run gauss and laplace (catch errors per method and show them in that method's column without breaking the other).
2. Elements table: rows a, e, i, Ω, ω, M (at a common epoch = middle obs TT), q, period; columns Gauss | Laplace (classical) | Laplace (refined) | Catalog | errors (abs and %, color-coded). Catalog elements must be propagated to the same epoch (mean anomaly advanced by n·Δt) before comparison — state this in the UI.
3. Residuals: for each method, re-predict RA/Dec at the 3 observation times and show O−C in arcsec.
4. Forward prediction: predicted RA/Dec for 7/30/90 days later from each solution vs catalog, angular difference in arcmin — the 'did we find it again?' payoff.
5. Root picker: if rootsConsidered.length>1, show the roots and let the user re-run with rootIndex.
6. Warnings & convergence flags from IODResult displayed.
7. Tests (jsdom): render with a synthetic noiseless Ceres set; assert error cells for a are < 1e-4 %.
acceptance_criteria: With a synthetic Ceres set the page shows both solutions with errors near zero; with a malformed set it shows the validation error; multiple-root case lets the user pick a root; npm test & build green.
notes: From orbits-q9e.8 review: Gauss can return two surviving roots that both pass vetting (Eros testDate+90d: default pick wrong, a off ~3x). Solve page MUST surface multi-root warning prominently and show all surviving candidates side-by-side. From orbits-q9e.11 review: Solve page must itself check set.observations.length===3 (importSet currently accepts any length) and show 'incomplete set' otherwise. Use '@astro' import alias.

title: Observe page: enter 3 observations, site manager, and synthetic-observation generator
description:
INPUT: app shell/store, astro angles/time, ephemeris predictor + catalog.
STEPS:
1. src/ui/pages/ObservePage.tsx: choose/create an observation set; three observation rows each with: date+time UTC (datetime-local input interpreted as UTC, labelled clearly), RA (text, accepts formats of parseRA), Dec (text, parseDec), site dropdown (or 'geocenter'). Show parsed value echo (e.g. '12h 34m 56.0s') and inline errors from the parser.
2. Site manager: add site by name/lat/lon/elevation; 'Use my location' button via navigator.geolocation (handle denial gracefully with a message).
3. Show set-level validation from validateObservations (errors block solving, warnings shown in amber).
4. Synthetic generator panel: pick catalog body, start date, spacing (days, default 7), site, noise sigma (arcsec, default 0, seeded RNG with displayed seed) -> fills the three rows using predict(). Label the set 'synthetic' so the Solve page can show it.
5. 'Solve this set' button navigates to /solve with the active set.
6. Tests (jsdom + testing-library): entering valid values persists to store; '25 00 00' RA shows error; synthetic generator for Ceres produces 3 obs whose RA matches predict() at noise 0.
acceptance_criteria: Component tests cover valid entry, each validation error, synthetic generation with seeded noise, and persistence; npm test & build green.

title: App shell: routing, layout, zustand store with persisted sites/observations
description:
INPUT: scaffold. No dependency on astro math beyond types (import types only from @astro/iod/types if present; otherwise define a local Observation type matching the IOD types task: { jdUtc, raRad, decRad, site, label? } — FLAG: reconcile if both exist).
STEPS:
1. src/ui/App.tsx with HashRouter routes: '/' (Home/intro), '/plan', '/observe', '/solve', '/learn/gauss', '/learn/laplace', '/explore'. Each route gets a placeholder page component under src/ui/pages/ with a heading.
2. Responsive layout: top nav (collapses to a menu < 640px), main content area. Dark theme default (night-observing friendly), plus a 'red night mode' toggle that tints the UI red (CSS variables).
3. src/ui/store.ts (zustand + persist middleware, key 'orbits-v1'): sites: Site[] with named entries and a selectedSiteId; observationSets: {id,name,targetId?,observations: Observation[]}[]; activeSetId. Actions: add/update/remove for each; setActive.
4. Import/export: exportSet(id)->JSON string (schemaVersion:1); importSet(json) validates shape and rejects with a readable message.

title: Laplace method of IOD with optional iteration and full trace
description:
INPUT: same as the Gauss task (two-body, observer, ephemeris, IOD types/polynomial). Independent of gauss.ts — do not import from it.
STEPS:
1. src/astro/iod/laplace.ts: laplace(obs, opts?:{ iterate=true, maxIter=50, tol=1e-12, lightTime=true, rootIndex?:number }) -> IODResult.
2. Algorithm (classical Laplace, e.g. Escobal 'Methods of Orbit Determination' ch.7 or Danby ch.7): unit vectors L_i; Lagrange-interpolate L(t) at t2 to get L, L', L'' (second-order in time spacing, handle unequal spacing); observer R, R' and R'' at t2 (R'' = -mu R/|R|^3 for the heliocentric observer approx, R' from the Earth model plus observer rotation contribution); determinants D, D1, D2 (and Dij variants); polynomial in r2 (r^8 + a r^6 + b r^3 + c) solved with solveDistancePolynomial; rho, rho' -> r2, v2.
3. Iterative refinement (when opts.iterate): use r2,v2 to compute f,g at t1,t3 via lagrangeFG, re-solve rho2 with the Gauss-like linear system (document this is the 'Laplace with Leuschner/Gauss refinement' variant) OR re-fit L derivatives with light-time corrected times — choose one, document in a header comment. Mark the non-iterated result as trace step 'classical-result' so the UI can show raw Laplace vs refined.
4. Root selection policy identical to the Gauss task (rootIndex override, else largest elliptic root, warnings).
5. Trace step ids: 'los-vectors','interpolation','derivatives','observer-state','determinants','polynomial','roots','rho-rhodot','classical-result','iteration-<n>' (cap 20),'final-state','elements'.
6. Tests: noiseless synthetic (same setup as Gauss): with iterate=true a rel err <1e-5, e <1e-5, angles <1e-4 rad; with iterate=false a rel err <5% for 10-day spacing (classical Laplace is approximate). Noise test (1 arcsec, seeded): record a error and assert it is finite & < 20%.
acceptance_criteria: Synthetic noiseless test recovers elements within the stated tolerances; noise test documents the Gauss vs Laplace error ratio; trace contains every documented step id; npm test green.
notes: Implementation deviates from step 2 text by design (reviewed): R' and R'' come from the same 3-point Lagrange fit as L, not analytic Earth velocity + rotation; analytic version was inconsistent for topocentric sites. Iterated Laplace converges to the same fixed point as Gauss; method differences show only in the classical result.

title: Gauss method of IOD with iterative refinement and full trace
description:
INPUT: two-body core, observer positions, ephemeris predictor (for synthetic data), IOD types/polynomial.
STEPS:
1. src/astro/iod/gauss.ts: gauss(obs: IODInput, opts?:{ maxIter=50, tol=1e-12, lightTime=true, rootIndex?:number }) -> IODResult.
2. Algorithm (Curtis 'Orbital Mechanics for Engineering Students' Alg. 5.5 + 5.6, heliocentric): line-of-sight unit vectors L_i from RA/Dec; observer heliocentric R_i (observerHeliocentric with TT/UTC conversion); τ1, τ3, τ; D0 and Dij scalars; A, B, E; polynomial coefficients a,b,c; roots via solveDistancePolynomial; choose root (if >1 positive root: pick the one giving a bound orbit with smallest |a-error|? NO — pick by default the root yielding e<1 and r>1.1 AU-ish? Flag: use opts.rootIndex if provided, else the root with the largest r2 that yields an elliptic orbit, and record all candidates in rootsConsidered + warning). Initial f,g from series; r1,r2,r3 from slant ranges; v2 via f,g; then iterative improvement: exact f,g via universal variables (lagrangeFG), recompute c1,c3 and ranges, light-time correct observation times (t_i - rho_i/c) each iteration; stop when |Δrho|<tol or maxIter (converged=false + warning).
3. Emit trace steps with ids: 'los-vectors','observer-positions','time-intervals','d-scalars','polynomial','roots','slant-ranges','initial-orbit','iteration-<n>' (cap stored iterations at 20),'final-state','elements'. Values must include rho_i, r_i vectors, f,g, sector-to-triangle ratios y1,y3 when available.
4. Tests (synthetic, noiseless): pick 3 dates 10 days apart around each body's epoch, generate obs with predict() (geocentric AND a topocentric site), run gauss, compare elements to catalog: a rel err <1e-6, e abs <1e-6, angles <1e-5 rad (because the same Earth model is used, recovery should be near exact). Plus a degraded test: 1-arcsec Gaussian noise (seeded) gives a within 2%.
EDGE: degenerate geometry (D0≈0) -> throw Error('Observations are nearly coplanar with the Sun-observer geometry; choose different times').
acceptance_criteria: Synthetic test recovers a,e,i,Ω,ω,M within the stated tolerances for Ceres, Vesta, Eros; trace contains every documented step id; npm test green.

title: IOD shared types, trace schema, and 8th-degree distance polynomial root finder
description:
INPUT: astro core.
STEPS:
1. src/astro/iod/types.ts: Observation = { jdUtc, raRad, decRad, site: Site|null, label? }. IODInput = [Observation,Observation,Observation] (must be strictly increasing in time). IODResult = { method:'gauss'|'laplace', elements: OrbitalElements, r2:Vec3, v2:Vec3, jdTt2, rootsConsidered:number[], chosenRoot:number, iterations:number, converged:boolean, warnings:string[], trace: TraceStep[] }.
2. TraceStep = { id:string, title:string, explanation:string (1-3 sentences plain English, may contain simple TeX between $...$), values: Record<string, number|number[]|Vec3> }. This is what the walkthrough visualizations replay; document the expected step ids in a comment (each method task will fill them).
3. src/astro/iod/validate.ts: validateObservations(obs) -> throws descriptive Errors for: not exactly 3 obs, non-increasing times, any two obs < 0.5 day apart (warning, not error), total arc > 120 days (warning), identical directions (error).
4. src/astro/iod/polynomial.ts: solveDistancePolynomial(a,b,c) -> sorted positive real roots of r^8 + a r^6 + b r^3 + c = 0. Use companion-matrix-free approach: bracket sign changes on a log-spaced grid r in [1e-3, 1e3] (≥2000 samples) then refine each bracket with Brent/bisection-Newton to |f|<1e-14 scaled. Also return Descartes' rule-of-signs count for display.
5. Tests: construct polynomials from known roots (e.g. Curtis Example 5.11 numbers, or synthetic); verify roots and that no spurious roots are reported; validation error cases.
acceptance_criteria: Types compile; root finder finds all positive real roots of r^8 + a r^6 + b r^3 + c for documented test polynomials to 1e-12 relative; npm test green.

title: Ephemeris predictor: elements -> astrometric topocentric RA/Dec with light-time and magnitude
description:
INPUT: two-body core, Earth/observer module, catalog.json and Horizons fixtures.
STEPS:
1. src/astro/ephemeris.ts: predict(body: OrbitalElements | {planet:string}, jdUtc, site|null) -> { raRad, decRad, deltaAu (observer distance), rHelioAu, phaseAngleRad, lightTimeDays, rObserver:Vec3, rBody:Vec3 }.
2. Astrometric light-time: iterate tau = |r_body(t - tau) - R_obs(t)|/c until |Δtau|<1e-10 d (max 10 iters). No aberration/deflection (astrometric matches Horizons QUANTITIES=1 convention).
3. src/astro/magnitude.ts: hgMagnitude(H,G,r,delta,phase) per IAU H-G system (Bowell 1989). Test with a hand-computed case.
4. src/astro/catalog.ts: loadCatalog() reads @data/catalog.json and converts degrees to OrbitalElements (radians, frame eclipticJ2000); resolve planet entries via planets module.
5. Tests: for each fixture file, for every 5th row, |angular separation(predicted, Horizons)| < 60 arcsec. Log the max error found (console.info) so the reviewer can see headroom. Use a proper great-circle separation function (add angularSeparation to angles.ts if missing).
EDGE: if a fixture is absent, the test must fail (not skip) — fixtures are a hard dependency of this task.
acceptance_criteria: Predicted RA/Dec for Ceres/Vesta/Eros match Horizons fixtures within 60 arcsec (geocentric and site 568) over the fixture windows; magnitude function tested; npm test green.

title: Fetch bundled datasets: JPL SBDB elements catalog + Horizons golden RA/Dec fixtures
description:
INPUT: scaffold only (no astro code needed). Requires network (curl) at dev time; the app never fetches at runtime.
STEPS:
1. Write scripts/fetch-data.mjs (Node 18+, built-in fetch, no deps) runnable via 'npm run fetch-data'.
2. Catalog: for bodies [1 Ceres, 2 Pallas, 3 Juno, 4 Vesta, 6 Hebe, 7 Iris, 10 Hygiea, 433 Eros] query https://ssd-api.jpl.nasa.gov/sbdb.api?sstr=<number>&phys-par=1 . Write src/data/catalog.json: [{ id, name, kind:'asteroid', epochJdTt, a, e, iDeg, OmegaDeg, omegaDeg, MDeg, H, G (default 0.15 if absent), source:'JPL SBDB', fetchedAt ISO }]. Angles in J2000 ecliptic degrees as SBDB provides. Also add planet entries {id:'mars'|'jupiter'|'saturn', kind:'planet', source:'Standish'} with no elements (resolved at runtime by the planets module).
3. Horizons fixtures via https://ssd.jpl.nasa.gov/api/horizons.api (format=json, EPHEM_TYPE=OBSERVER, QUANTITIES='1,20' i.e. astrometric RA/Dec + range, ANG_FORMAT=DEG, CSV_FORMAT=YES, TIME_TYPE=UT). For Ceres, Vesta and Eros produce: (a) geocentric (CENTER='500@399') daily positions for a 40-day window centered within ±30 days of that body's SBDB epoch; (b) one topocentric set for MPC site 568 (Mauna Kea) for the same window. Parse the CSV between $$SOE/$$EOE into tests/fixtures/horizons/<name>-<center>.json: { body, center, timeScale:'UTC', rows:[{jdUtc, raDeg, decDeg, deltaAu}] , query: <full URL> }.
4. Earth fixture: Horizons VECTORS for Earth (COMMAND='399', CENTER='500@10', REF_PLANE=FRAME (equatorial J2000), OUT_UNITS=AU-D) yearly 2000-2050 -> tests/fixtures/horizons/earth.json {rows:[{jdTdb,x,y,z,vx,vy,vz}]}.
5. Add src/data/catalog.schema.test.ts and tests/fixtures/fixtures.test.ts that check field presence, numeric ranges (0<=e<1, 0<a<10, angles in [0,360)), and rows.length>=40.
ERROR HANDLING: script retries each request up to 3 times with backoff, fails loudly (non-zero exit) on missing $$SOE markers or HTTP errors; never writes partial files (write to temp then rename).
AMBIGUITY: if SBDB field names differ from expectations, map them explicitly and note the mapping in a comment in the script.
acceptance_criteria: src/data/catalog.json and tests/fixtures/horizons/*.json exist, conform to the documented schema, and a schema test validates them; the fetch script is re-runnable.

title: Earth & planet heliocentric positions (Standish) plus observer topocentric offset
description:
INPUT: src/astro core + two-body core (elementsToState / Kepler).
STEPS:
1. src/astro/planets.ts: embed JPL Standish 'Keplerian Elements for Approximate Positions of the Major Planets' Table 1 (valid 1800-2050): a, e, I, L, long.peri, long.node and their per-century rates for Mercury..Neptune and EM Bary. Source URL in a comment: https://ssd.jpl.nasa.gov/planets/approx_pos.html . Function planetHeliocentric(name, jdTt) -> {r,v} J2000 equatorial AU, AU/day (velocity via elementsToState with the instantaneous elements). Throw outside 1800-2050.
2. earthHeliocentric(jdTt) = EM Bary from the same table (document the ~3e-5 AU Moon offset as accepted error).
3. src/astro/observer.ts: type Site = {latDeg, lonEastDeg, elevM}; observerGeocentric(site, jdUtc) -> Vec3 in AU, J2000 equatorial, using WGS84 geodetic->geocentric and rotation by LST (ignore precession/nutation between date and J2000 — document this simplification; error <1e-7 AU-scale effect on parallax direction is acceptable). observerHeliocentric(site,jdTt,jdUtc) = earth + geocentric. A null site means the geocenter.
4. Tests: Sun geocentric RA/Dec = -earthHeliocentric, compare with Meeus Ex.25.a (1992 Oct 13 0h TD: RA 13h13m31.4s, Dec -7°47'06") within 0.02°; |observerGeocentric| ≈ 6378 km at equator site; Earth orbital speed ~0.0172 AU/day.
5. If tests/fixtures/horizons/earth.json exists (produced by the data-fetch task) add a comparison test; otherwise skip that test with it.skipIf and a comment.
acceptance_criteria: Earth heliocentric position matches the Horizons Earth fixture within 2e-4 AU over 2000-2050 (if fixture available) or Meeus Ex.25.b Sun position within 0.01°; observer offset tests pass; npm test green.

title: Two-body core: Kepler solver, elements<->state vectors, universal-variable propagation
description:
INPUT: src/astro core (vec, constants, frames).
STEPS:
1. src/astro/elements.ts: type OrbitalElements = { a, e, i, Omega, omega, M0, epochJd, frame:'eclipticJ2000' } (angles radians, a in AU; for hyperbolic a<0). Also derived helpers: periodDays, perihelionQ, meanMotion, timeOfPerihelion.
2. src/astro/kepler.ts: solveKeplerElliptic(M,e) (Newton with Danby starter, |ΔE|<1e-14, max 50 iters, throw on non-convergence), solveKeplerHyperbolic(M,e). Test e in {0,0.1,0.5,0.9,0.99} and hyperbolic e=1.5.
3. src/astro/state.ts: elementsToState(el, jdTt, mu=GM_SUN) -> {r:Vec3, v:Vec3} in J2000 EQUATORIAL (compute in ecliptic, then rotate). stateToElements(r,v,jdTt,mu) -> OrbitalElements in ecliptic J2000. EDGE CASES: circular (e<1e-10: omega=0, M measured from node), equatorial (i<1e-10: Omega=0), both; e≈1 should not NaN (return parabola-adjacent best effort, flag in a 'warnings' array).
4. src/astro/propagate.ts: universal-variable Kepler propagation propagate(r0,v0,dtDays,mu) using Stumpff functions C(z),S(z) (series for |z|<1e-6), plus lagrangeFG(r0,v0,dt) returning {f,g,fdot,gdot}. Works for negative dt.
5. Tests: (a) elements->state->elements round trip relative error <1e-10 on random elliptic orbits (seeded RNG, 200 cases); (b) propagate a full period returns to start within 1e-9 AU; (c) propagate vs elementsToState at a later time agree within 1e-10 AU; (d) Curtis Example 3.7 / 4.3-style published numbers if convenient (convert units) — optional.
acceptance_criteria: Round-trip and propagation tests pass at the stated tolerances for elliptic, near-parabolic and hyperbolic cases; npm test green.

title: Astro core: constants, vectors, angles, time scales, frames, sidereal time
description:
INPUT: scaffold (src/astro). Pure TS, no DOM.
STEPS:
1. src/astro/constants.ts: GAUSS_K=0.01720209895, GM_SUN=k^2 (AU^3/day^2), AU_KM=149597870.700, C_AU_PER_DAY=173.1446326846693, OBLIQUITY_J2000_RAD = 84381.448 arcsec, EARTH_RADIUS_KM=6378.137, EARTH_FLATTENING=1/298.257223563, J2000_JD=2451545.0.
2. src/astro/vec.ts: type Vec3=[number,number,number]; add, sub, scale, dot, cross, norm, unit, rotateX, rotateZ. Unit-test cross/dot identities.
3. src/astro/angles.ts: deg/rad conversions; normalize to [0,2π); parseRA('hh mm ss.s' | 'hh:mm:ss.s' | decimal hours) -> radians; parseDec('±dd mm ss' | '±dd:mm:ss' | decimal deg) -> radians; formatRA/formatDec back to sexagesimal with configurable precision. EDGE CASES: '-00 30 00' must be negative; reject minutes/seconds >= 60, RA hours >= 24, |Dec| > 90 by throwing a descriptive Error.
4. src/astro/time.ts: calendar UTC (Date or y,m,d,h,m,s) -> JD(UTC); jdUtcToTt using a hard-coded leap-second table (1972-2017, TAI-UTC=37 s since 2017-01-01) + 32.184 s; dates before 1972 throw. jdToCalendar inverse. Test: Meeus Ex.7.a (1957 Oct 4.81 -> JD 2436116.31), round-trip.
5. src/astro/frames.ts: eclipticToEquatorial / equatorialToEcliptic (J2000 obliquity, rotation about X); radecToUnit(ra,dec)->Vec3 and unitToRadec. Round-trip tests.
6. src/astro/sidereal.ts: gmst(jdUt1) (IAU 1982 / Meeus 12.4, treat UT1≈UTC), lst(jd, lonEastRad). Test Meeus Ex.12.a (1987 Apr 10 0h UT -> 13h10m46.3668s) within 0.01 s.
7. src/astro/horizon.ts: equatorialToHorizontal(ra,dec,lst,lat)->{alt,az} (az from North through East). Test against Meeus Ex.13.b within 0.01°.
8. Export everything from src/astro/index.ts.
acceptance_criteria: All functions listed exist in src/astro with unit tests; tests reproduce the cited Meeus examples within the stated tolerances; npm test green.

title: Scaffold Vite+React+TS project with Vitest, ESLint, and folder layout
description:

title: Explore page: noise & spacing sensitivity of Gauss vs Laplace
description:
INPUT: gauss(), laplace(), predict(), catalog, app shell.
STEPS:
1. src/astro/sensitivity.ts (pure): sweep({bodyId, startJd, spacings:number[] days, noiseArcsec:number[], trials:number, seed, site}) -> grid of {spacing, noise, gaussAErrMedian, laplaceAErrMedian, gaussFailRate, laplaceFailRate}. Seeded PRNG (mulberry32), Box-Muller noise applied to RA·cos(Dec) and Dec.
2. Run sweeps in a Web Worker (src/ui/workers/sweep.worker.ts, Vite worker import) so UI stays responsive; show progress.
3. src/ui/pages/ExplorePage.tsx: controls (body, spacing range, noise range, trials ≤ 50, seed); two SVG heatmaps (Gauss, Laplace) of median relative error in a (log color scale) plus a line chart at fixed noise vs spacing. Legend and axis labels required.
4. Short text interpreting the result ('Laplace degrades faster for short arcs / high noise' — but only claim what the data on screen shows; phrase as an observation to look for).
5. Tests: sensitivity.ts determinism for fixed seed; zero-noise median errors ≈ 0 for Gauss; failure counting when a method throws.
acceptance_criteria: Explore page renders a sweep for a catalog body; sweep logic lives in a pure tested module; results are deterministic for a given seed; npm test & build green.
notes: From q9e.9: iterated Laplace == Gauss exactly (same fixed point). The sensitivity sweep must compare Gauss vs CLASSICAL Laplace (iterate=false), plus optionally Gauss's first approximation (trace 'initial-orbit'); comparing iterated Laplace to Gauss shows nothing.
